subject: Throughput warranty, measurement harness & pricing mapping for Dedicated GPU pool
messages:
From: Morgan Lewis <morgan@acmeai.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: procurement@acmeai.com
Date: 2026-10-12T15:03:00Z
Subject: Dedicated throughput warranty questions + pricing mapping

Ben —

Thanks for the demo yesterday. As we think about a committed Dedicated GPU pool, procurement and our infra team want clarity on two things before legal will sign: (1) the throughput warranty we can expect (tokens/sec and requests/sec) for our expected workload, and (2) how shortfalls are measured and credited back against our reserved commit.

Short background: our primary workload is a multi-turn assistant with an average request size (prompt + context) of ~120 tokens and median generated tokens of 40. Traffic profile: 60% short assistant responses (<=50 generated tokens), 30% longer explanations (~200 tokens), 10% embeddings/rerankers. We target p95 latency < 300ms for short responses and want a committed baseline of 25k generated tokens/sec across the pool (we estimate this maps to ~150 rps at our mix).

Specific asks:
- How does Redwood define tokens/sec for Dedicated (do you count generated tokens only, or generated + input tokens)?
- What measurement harness will you run for acceptance/ongoing SLA? Warmup, steady-state window durations, sample workload generation?
- If your observed tokens/sec is below the warranty, how are credits calculated vs discounts?
- Can you map committed capacity (GPU pool sizing / vCPU/GPU count) to expected tokens/sec and expected p95 latency targets at our sequence-length distribution?

Can you share a proposed acceptance and measurement plan we can pass to procurement and infra? Also include any place-holder billing language so we can model P&L while legal drafts the contract.

Appreciate it — Morgan
Morgan Lewis
Head of Platform
AcmeAI
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lewis <morgan@acmeai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-13T09:18:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput warranty questions + pricing mapping

Morgan —

Thanks for the clear notes and the traffic breakdown — that helps a lot. High level answers up front, details and a proposed validation plan below.

High level
- Tokens/sec definition: for Dedicated warranties we measure generated tokens/sec (model outputs) by default. Input/prompt tokens are reported separately for billing and debugging, but the warranty focuses on generated throughput since that aligns with GPU kernel time.
- Measurement harness: we propose a joint validation run using Redwood's validation harness (attached runbook v1) driven by a representative request generator you approve. Warmup = 30 minutes, steady-state sampling = 6 hours for contractual acceptance; for monthly SLA sampling we'll use daily 4-hour steady-state windows during peak traffic for ongoing verification.
- Credits vs discounts: our commercial approach is to apply pro-rata credits against the monthly reserved commit when observed tokens/sec in the acceptance window is below the agreed baseline. Formula and examples below.
- Mapping to pool size: we can provide a sizing table that maps GPU type + pool size -> expected tokens/sec and p95 latencies for your request mix. That table will be calibrated by an initial on-prem/real-workload run and validated during acceptance.

Proposed acceptance & measurement plan (summary)
1) Build representative workload: use your telemetry (we can accept a 24-hr sample or you can run our generator against a staging snapshot). We will translate into three request classes: SHORT (<=50 gen tokens), MEDIUM (~200 gen tokens), LONG (>512 gen tokens).
2) Warmup: 30 minutes of progressive ramp from 10% to 100% of target concurrency to populate KV cache + JIT/Kernels.
3) Steady-state: 6 continuous hours at agreed target arrival distribution; collect per-minute tokens/sec, p50/p95/p99 latencies, GPU utilization and queue depth.
4) Measurement rules: drop first 10 minutes post ramp for transient artifacts; require at least 5 consecutive minutes with no infra incidents. Tokens/sec is measured as sum(generated_tokens)/window. Latencies computed per request end-to-end at the API gateway.
5) Acceptance criteria: observed median tokens/sec >= 98% of baseline AND p95 latency targets met for SHORT class. If throughput shortfall exists but latency is within target, parties will review model config/quantization and retry up to one retest window.

Credit formula (illustrative)
- Let B = baseline tokens/sec (committed), O = observed tokens/sec (steady-state), M = monthly reserved commit value in USD.
- If O >= B -> no credit. If O < B -> credit = ((B - O) / B) * M * K, where K is an operational factor (default K=0.75) that reflects partial mitigation paths (burst capacity, fallback routing).
- Example: B=25k, O=22.5k -> shortfall=10% -> credit = 0.10 * M * 0.75 = 7.5% of monthly commit credited.

Attachments: redwood_throughput_runbook_v1.odt (validation steps), validation-harness-spec.csv (sample generator), placeholder billing language included in runbook.

Next steps
- If this approach looks sane to you, let's schedule a 60-min joint session (infra + Redwood infra engs + perf SMEs) to lock the request classes and calendar a 6-hour acceptance run.

I'll also loop Marissa and Priyom for the sizing table; Marissa will propose the initial GPU mapping (type/count) based on your latency targets.

Ben
Ben Carter | Senior Sales Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Morgan Lewis <morgan@acmeai.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-10-14T13:40:00Z
Subject: Re: Dedicated throughput warranty questions + pricing mapping

Morgan — quick tech clarifications and the explicit measurement semantics we apply.

Tokens/sec definition (expanded)- We measure generated tokens/sec (G) for warranty calculations. We log input tokens (I) and total tokens (T = I + G) for observability. For workload translation we report both G and T in the sizing table, but credits/SLAs are evaluated on G. This is because GPU kernel time maps closely with generated token compute, particularly for autoregressive decoders.

KV cache / cold-start effects- Measurement windows must include a warmup (we suggested 30m) to pre-populate KV cache and allow kernel heuristics to stabilize. We explicitly discard the warmup window and the first 10 minutes of steady-state for transient effects (as Ben noted). If your workload has heavy context-shift (many unique conversation IDs), we'll add an additional cold-start subtest.

Latency targets and measurement- Short class (<=50 gen tokens): p95 API-to-response < 300ms measured at edge (includes network within same region).- Medium class (~200 gen tokens): p95 < 700ms.
- We sample latencies per request and report p50/p95/p99 across steady-state window. If p95 > target but tokens/sec meets baseline, we treat as a severity-2 operational item and run remediation (batching config, kernel selector). Repeated misses can be grounds for additional credits per contract.

SLA sample math and billing mapping (concrete example)
- Baseline B = 25,000 G/s; steady-state window = 6h. If average observed across steady window O_avg < 0.95*B -> 1x credit. If O_avg between 0.95*B and 0.98*B -> 0.5x credit. If O_avg >= 0.98*B -> no credit.
- Credit unit = pro-rata dollar credit on the monthly reserved commit (makes it easy for procurement modeling).
- If missed months > 2 in a rolling 6 month period, we will offer a one-time remediation package (performance tuning + 1-week elevated support) and extend rebate discussions.

Sizing note (initial guidance)
- For your mix: SHORT 60%, MED 30%, LONG 10% -> preliminary mapping on A100-style pool: 4x A100s -> ~18-30k G/s depending on quantization profile and avg output tokens. 8x A100s -> comfortably above 40k G/s. We will provide a calibrated table once you approve the validation harness.

Operational asks for acceptance run
1) Provide a 24-hr sampling of real telemetry (if possible) or approve our synthetic distribution in validation-harness-spec.csv.
2) Confirm the region (you listed us region — we'll run both staging and us-east-1 runs).
3) Agree on a single acceptance date window; preferred dates I have next week: Tue 10/20 or Thu 10/22.

If procurement needs a placeholder clause for the order form, we've included a short paragraph in the runbook that mirrors the formula above (credit ladder + retest clause). Happy to iterate.

Marissa
Marissa Cole | Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Thanks Ben/Marissa — this is very helpful and actionable. A few quick items:

1) Procurement likes the pro-rata credit approach (makes the financial model simple). Can you also provide an example clause we can paste into our SOW template?
2) We'd like to request a 10% one-time onboarding discount on the first three months of the reserved commit in exchange for a 12-month upfront commit. Would Redwood consider that (we're happy to include it as a commercial term rather than an SLA matter).
3) 10/22 works for us for the acceptance run. Please send a calendar invite with the test owner list and run checklist.

If you send the SOW clause and a calendar invite I'll get the procurement sign-off and lock the commitment.

Best — Morgan
